passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: Management’s discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations is provided as a supplement to, and should be read in conjunction with, the consolidated financial statements and related notes to enhance the understanding of the Company’s operations and present business environment. Components of management’s discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations include: • Overview • Analysis of Operations • Result of Operations • Segment Results • Outlook • Liquidity and Capital Resources • Recent Accounting Pronouncements • Critical Accounting Estimates • Long-Term Employee Benefits • Environmental Matters OVERVIEW As of December 31, 2025, the Company has $1.7 billion of net working capital and $0.7 billion in cash and cash equivalents. The Company expects its cash and cash equivalents, cash generated from operations, and ability to access the debt capital markets to provide sufficient liquidity and financial flexibility to meet the liquidity requirements associated with its continued operations. The Company continually assesses its liquidity position, including possible sources of incremental liquidity, in light of the current economic environment, capital market conditions and Company performance. Electronics Separation On November 1, 2025, the Company completed the separation of its semiconductor and interconnect solutions businesses, (the "Electronics Business" and the separation of the Electronics Business, the “Electronics Separation”) into an independent public company, Qnity Electronics, Inc. (“Qnity”), by way of the distribution to DuPont's stockholders of record as of October 22, 2025, of all the issued and outstanding common stock of Qnity on November 1, 2025 (the “Qnity Distribution”). As a result, the financial results of the divested Electronics Business are reflected in DuPont's Consolidated Financial Statements as discontinued operations, along with comparative periods. Aramids Divestiture On August 29, 2025, DuPont announced a definitive agreement to sell the Aramids business (the “Aramids Divestiture”) to Arclin, a portfolio company of an affiliate of TJC LP, (“TJC”), in return for pre-tax cash proceeds of approximately $1.2 billion, subject to customary transaction adjustments, a note receivable in the principal amount of $300 million and a non-controlling common equity interest (the "Aramids Equity Consideration"), valued at $325 million in the future Arclin holding company that will hold the Arclin global materials business and the Aramids business being divested. The transaction is expected to close around the end of the first quarter 2026, subject to customary closing conditions and receipt of regulatory approvals. As a result, the financial results of the Aramids business being divested are reflected in DuPont's Consolidated Financial Statements as discontinued operations, along with comparative periods. 2025 Segment Realignments Effective in the first quarter of 2025, in preparation for the Electronics Separation, the Company realigned its management and reporting structure. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: The Company's operations could be affected by various risks, many of which are beyond its control. Based on current information, the Company believes that the following identifies the most material risk factors that could affect its operations. Past financial performance may not be a reliable indicator of future performance and historical trends should not be used to anticipate results or trends in future periods. Risks Relating to the Qnity Distribution, M&M Divestitures, N&B Transaction, the DWDP Distributions and the Aramids Divestiture If the Qnity Distribution, together with certain related transactions, including the cash distribution Qnity made to DuPont prior to the Qnity Distribution, were to fail to qualify for non-recognition treatment for U.S. federal income tax purposes, then DuPont could be subject to significant tax liability. DuPont received an opinion of counsel as a condition to the Qnity Distribution, in form and substance acceptable to DuPont, substantially to the effect that, among other things, the Qnity Distribution along with certain related transactions will qualify for non-recognition treatment under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the “Code”, and such opinion, the “Tax Opinion”). The Tax Opinion relied on certain facts, assumptions, and undertakings, and certain representations from DuPont and Qnity, regarding the past and future conduct of each of their respective businesses and other matters. Notwithstanding the receipt of the Tax Opinion, the Internal Revenue Service (the “IRS”) could determine on audit that the Qnity Distribution and/or certain related transactions should be treated as taxable transactions if it determines that any of these facts, assumptions, representations or undertakings are not correct or have been violated, or that the Qnity Distribution should be taxable for other reasons, including if the IRS were to disagree with the conclusions of the Tax Opinion. If the Qnity Distribution and/or certain related transactions fail to qualify for tax-free treatment under U.S. federal, state and local tax law and/or foreign tax law, it is expected that DuPont could incur significant tax liabilities under U.S. federal, state, local and/or foreign tax law. Generally, corporate taxes resulting from the failure of the Qnity Distribution to qualify for tax-free treatment for U.S. federal income tax purposes would be imposed on DuPont. Under the Tax Matters Agreement, effective as of November 1, 2025, between DuPont and Qnity (the “Electronics Tax Matters Agreement”), the responsibility for such taxes may be allocated between DuPont and Qnity under certain circumstances and each of DuPont and Qnity may be obligated to indemnify the other against any such taxes imposed on it. To the extent that DuPont is responsible for any liability as a result of the failure of the Qnity Distribution and/or certain related transactions to qualify for non-recognition treatment for U.S. federal income tax purposes, there could be a material adverse impact on DuPont’s business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows in subsequent reporting periods. credit_strengths.text: Gross leverage fell sharply year over year, reflecting debt repayment alongside modest EBITDA growth, and now sits comfortably inside the intermediate risk band with meaningful headroom to the next threshold. This deleveraging trajectory is the single strongest credit positive for the issuer.

Liquidity is solid: cash plus net working capital comfortably cover near-term obligations, and the current ratio exceeds the sector median. Management explicitly cites cash, operating generation and debt capital market access as sufficient to fund continued operations and separation-related needs.

key_risks.text: Interest coverage is thin in absolute terms and far below the sector median, having improved only modestly year over year. Operating income covers interest expense by a narrow margin, leaving little cushion if margins compress or refinancing costs rise, which is a material constraint on the credit profile.

The Qnity Distribution carries contingent tax exposure: if the separation fails non-recognition treatment, DuPont could face significant tax liabilities, with allocation and indemnity governed by the Tax Matters Agreement. This is a discrete, potentially large cash call not captured in reported leverage.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Debt service rests on EBITDA rather than operating cash flow, which is unavailable in the bundle, so free cash flow coverage of debt and distributions cannot be assessed. EBITDA covers interest several times over, but the absence of cash flow data is a material gap for judging true servicing capacity.

The maturity profile is benign near term, with no scheduled repayments in the next two years and the bulk of debt falling due in year three. That runway gives the issuer time to refinance from a position of reduced leverage, though the concentration warrants monitoring.

overall_credit_view.text: The credit profile is intermediate: leverage has deleveraged materially and sits below the prior year but above the sector median, while coverage remains well below peers. Deleveraging and solid liquidity offset weak interest coverage, supporting a stable but not strong standing.

Portfolio reshaping via the Electronics Separation and pending Aramids Divestiture simplifies the business and brings proceeds, but dividends absorb a meaningful share of cash uses and contingent separation tax risk persists. Our forward view is that leverage stays manageable absent large distributions or adverse tax outcomes.

credit_strengths.text: 總槓桿按年大幅下降，反映債務償還加上EBITDA溫和增長，現時穩處於中間風險區間，距下一門檻仍有充裕緩衝。此去槓桿軌跡是發行人最強勁的單一信用正面因素。
流動性穩健：現金加淨營運資金足以覆蓋短期債務，流動比率高於行業中位數。管理層明確指出現金、經營現金產生及債務資本市場渠道足以支持持續經營及分拆相關需要。

key_risks.text: 利息覆蓋率絕對水平偏薄，且遠低於行業中位數，按年僅溫和改善。經營溢利僅以狹窄幅度覆蓋利息開支，若利潤率受壓或再融資成本上升，緩衝空間有限，對信用狀況構成重大制約。
Qnity分派附帶或然稅務風險：若分拆未能符合不確認處理，DuPont可能面臨重大稅務負債，其分攤及彌償由稅務事項協議規管。此為一項獨立、可能金額龐大的現金需求，並未反映於呈報槓桿之中。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 償債能力取決於EBITDA而非經營現金流，惟後者未載於本資料包內，故無法評估自由現金流對債務及分派的覆蓋。EBITDA覆蓋利息數倍，但缺乏現金流數據是判斷真實償債能力的重大缺口。
短期到期結構溫和，未來兩年並無預定還款，大部分債務於第三年到期。此緩衝期讓發行人可在槓桿降低的基礎上進行再融資，惟集中度值得監察。

overall_credit_view.text: 信用狀況屬中等：槓桿已大幅去槓桿，低於上年但高於行業中位數，而覆蓋率仍遠低於同業。去槓桿及穩健流動性抵銷了疲弱的利息覆蓋，支持穩定但非強勁的評級地位。
透過電子業務分拆及待完成的芳綸業務出售重塑組合，簡化業務並帶來所得款項，惟股息佔現金用途相當比重，且分拆的或然稅務風險仍然存在。我們的前瞻觀點是，在沒有大規模分派或不利稅務結果的情況下，槓桿維持可控。
